title: PET-CT scan
what: A small amount of radioactive sugar is given into a vein. The scanner shows where cells take it up most actively and combines this with a CT image.
why: Most often for cancer: to find affected areas, see how far it has spread, and check how treatment is working.
duration: usually 2 to 3 hours at the center; the scan itself takes 15 to 30 minutes
tell_doctor: Diabetes and your diabetes medicines. Your prep will be adjusted
If you are pregnant or breastfeeding
Allergy to contrast, or kidney disease
If it is hard for you to lie on your back for a long time, or you are afraid of closed spaces
The dates of your last chemotherapy or radiation therapy

prepare.title: Fasting
prepare.text: Usually no food for 4 to 6 hours. Only plain water without sugar. No chewing gum or sweets.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: For 24 hours, avoid hard exercise and physical work. You are often advised to eat fewer sweets and less bread and pasta. Your clinic will tell you more.

prepare.title: Diabetes
prepare.text: Your blood sugar should be normal. The doctor decides how to take your medicines that day.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Warm and comfortable, with no metal.

bring: Past CT, MRI, or PET images on a disc, and reports
steps: An IV is put into a vein and the tracer is given
For about an hour you sit or lie calmly in a quiet room: no talking, reading, or walking
Go to the toilet before the scan
You lie on the table, and it slowly moves through the scanner ring
feel: You do not feel the tracer going in
The scanner is not as loud as an MRI
If contrast is given, you may feel a wave of warmth through your body
after: Drink more water for the rest of the day. The tracer leaves faster with urine
You can usually eat right away
For a few hours, stay away from pregnant women and small children. Your clinic will tell you for how long
The report is usually ready in 1 to 3 days
red_flags: After the injection: a rash, a swollen face, or trouble breathing. Tell the staff right away or call emergency services

faq.q: Is the radiation from PET-CT dangerous?
faq.a: The dose is small and leaves the body quickly. The doctor orders the scan when the benefit is greater than the risk.

faq.q: Why can't I eat before a PET-CT?
faq.a: The tracer is a form of sugar. If you have eaten, your blood sugar is high and the images will be worse.

reminders.text: PET-CT tomorrow. No hard exercise or physical work today. Eat fewer sweets, and less bread and pasta.
PET-CT in 6 hours. Time to stop eating. Only plain water without sugar, unless your clinic said otherwise.
